subject.title: Add a Computer Use plugin manifest contract

question: Should OpenClaw add the proposed Computer Use provider manifest contract now, and what permission-binding metadata must it include before the macOS host can trust it?
rationale: The request adds plugin API surface that is read before runtime load and may inform Accessibility and Screen Recording permission binding, so code inspection alone cannot decide the permanent trust boundary.

options.title: Review and narrow the linked contract
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97939 as the implementation path, but require explicit validation, docs, tests, and security semantics before landing.

options.title: Defer until host binding design is complete
options.body: Keep the issue open but pause the manifest API until macOS host discovery and permission ownership requirements are fully specified.

options.title: Reject the manifest surface
options.body: Close the direction and keep Computer Use provider discovery runtime/plugin-owned if maintainers do not want static host permission metadata in manifests.

recommendation.title: Review and narrow the linked contract
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97939 as the implementation path, but require explicit validation, docs, tests, and security semantics before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest history signal on plugin manifest contract structure and provider metadata refactors.
